resources.string: Something tried passwords on your DeKoi. No ordinary device in a home does that.
Ordinary devices never pretend to be another device. This is how someone gets between your devices and the internet.
Some apps and network tools do this too. If you don’t recognise the device, treat it as an attack.
It comes from a device you marked as known, so it is most likely you or one of your own tools.
This is about your DeKoi itself, not an attack.
Find the device. It looks like a phone, tablet or watch, so check the ones people in your home and your guests carry.
Find the device. It looks like a computer, so check the laptops and desktops in your home.
Find the device. It looks like a TV, streaming box, speaker or games console, so check your living room and bedrooms.
Find the device. It looks like a printer or storage box, so check where you keep office equipment.
Find the device. It looks like a camera or a smart home device, such as a plug, bulb, thermostat or doorbell.
Find the device. It looks like network equipment, such as a router, Wi-Fi extender or network switch.
Find the device. Your router’s app or settings page lists the connected devices by their hardware address.
Ask who in your home owns it. On it, turn off Wi-Fi.
Unplug its network cable or turn off its Wi-Fi. Leave it switched on.
Unplug it or take out its batteries. Reset it and update its software before using it again.
Shut it down from its app or power button, then unplug its network cable, so no files are lost.
If you have more than one, unplug the extra ones one at a time. If this is the box from your internet provider, restart it instead.
If no one recognises it, block it in your router’s app or settings page by its hardware address.
Change your Wi-Fi password. Devices that don’t get the new password can no longer join.
Change the passwords of your important accounts, such as email and banking, from a device you trust.
Restart your router, so every device gets its network settings from the router again.
Check that your DeKoi has power. Its light should be on.
Check that its network cable is plugged in at both ends.
Wait a few minutes. It reconnects by itself and tells you when it is back.
Looks like a Wi-Fi access point
Looks like a smart home device
Looks like a watch or wearable
DeKoi can’t tell what this is yet
